entry.title: Nobel and Panofsky prizes
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Francis Halzen was awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. Separately, Fermilab's Sam Zeller received the W.K.H. Panofsky Prize for co-leading MicroBooNE, which advanced next-generation liquid-argon time projection chamber technology for neutrino detection.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab, CERN and SURF crews have started building the first of two cryostats, the large insulated containers that will hold liquid argon for DUNE. A separate Fermilab report on the start of construction in South Dakota notes that physicists at the University of Texas at Arlington are developing and building the field cage and other detector components.

entry.title: JUNO water purity
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. JUNO is a 20 kton liquid-scintillator detector designed primarily to determine the neutrino mass ordering. Because the scintillator is in direct contact with ultrapure water during filling, the water must have a radium concentration below 50 μBq/m3. A new paper describes a radium measurement system sensitive down to 3.9 μBq/m3 and an optimised 100 t/h production process that combines selective ion-exchange resin with membrane separation.

entry.title: Super-Kamiokande solar data
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The Super-Kamiokande Collaboration used 5805 days of 8B solar neutrino data from phases I to IV to constrain the Sun's core. The paper presents an outer bound on the solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the core. It uses the dependence of 8B production on core temperature and of adiabatic flavour conversion on the local electron density.

entry.title: ProtoDUNE muon seasonality
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The DUNE Collaboration measured the seasonal variation of the cosmic-ray muon rate in the ProtoDUNE single-phase detector at the CERN Neutrino Platform, using data from December 2018 to July 2020. The rate shows a seasonal modulation with a significance of 4σ relative to no variation, and it peaks in winter. This is consistent with measurements from other surface experiments with a low muon-energy threshold.

entry.title: SHiP oscillation sensitivity
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The SHiP Collaboration points out that its baseline detector configuration records neutrino interactions at two stations about 70 m apart: the scattering and neutrino detector, and the calorimeter system. This makes SHiP a two-baseline experiment for oscillations induced by a sterile neutrino. The study uses a Geant4 simulation of Genie-generated interactions to derive the energy response to electron- and muon-neutrino charged-current events and the rejection of neutral-current π0 background.

entry.title: ESSnuSB solar neutrinos
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The ESSnuSB Collaboration studied what its large underground water-Cherenkov detector could do for solar neutrinos. The two targets are the MSW spectral upturn in the 8B survival probability and the first direct observation of the rare hep flux. The analysis includes detector systematics and backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and 222Rn, and its discovery power rests on spectral shape rather than absolute rate.

entry.title: The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter that may contain
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper computes the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron-star matter that may contain Δ isobars. It points out that the specific contribution of this channel had not been worked out explicitly, although nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes are established as dominant cooling mechanisms. This matters for anyone modelling neutron-star cooling through neutrino emission.

entry.title: The authors ask whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cosmic-ray
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors ask whether kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could measure the primary cosmic-ray spectrum through the atmospheric neutrino flux. They report that such detectors can discriminate between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for cross-section and hadronic-interaction uncertainties. They also introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary spectrum, which is relevant to atmospheric-flux systematics.

entry.title: This work proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. This work proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations. Every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to the phase. A rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference, so decoherence-based searches have to look for that specific signature.

entry.title: The paper gives semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper gives semianalytic approximations for the quasisteady outcome of slow and fast flavour conversion in neutrino-dense environments. These are intended as subgrid inputs for supernova simulations that cannot include neutrino quantum kinetics. The authors report excellent agreement with multiangle and multienergy solutions of the kinetic equations, independent of the mass ordering.

entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study a gauged L_μ − L_τ ultralight vector boson that, through kinetic mixing with the photon, produces an extra matter potential inside the Sun. This modifies MSW flavour conversion, and the paper uses recent solar measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande, with prospects for JUNO and XLZD. It shows how solar neutrino oscillations can constrain new light mediators.

entry.title: The paper derives limits on anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models from solar neutrino–electron elastic scatte
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper derives limits on anomaly-free U(1)_X dark photon models from solar neutrino–electron elastic scattering in PandaX-4T and XENONnT. It covers six benchmark models and finds that the strength of the limits correlates with the leptonic charge assignments, and it also gives model-independent limits for pure kinetic and pure mass mixing. Dark-matter detectors thus act as low-energy neutrino-scattering experiments.
